quests.instruction: You want to know if today's lunch has nuts in it. Who in the cafeteria can tell you?
quests.hint: Think about who prepares the food.
quests.explanation: Cafeteria staff know what goes into each meal and can answer questions about ingredients.
quests.funFact: Food labels in many countries list common allergens such as milk, eggs, and nuts.

quests.instruction: You scraped your knee on the playground, and it is bleeding a little. Who should you ask for help?
quests.hint: This person has a first aid kit and training.
quests.explanation: A school nurse can clean and cover small injuries and decide whether more help is needed.
quests.funFact: Cleaning a scrape with clean water helps prevent infection.

quests.instruction: You don't understand how to do a math problem in class. Who is the best person to ask first?
quests.hint: Think about who is teaching the lesson.
quests.explanation: Your teacher knows what you're learning and can explain it in a way that helps.
quests.funFact: The word 'question' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to ask or seek'.

quests.instruction: A new rule is needed for how students enter the building safely. Who usually decides?
quests.hint: This person is responsible for the whole school.
quests.explanation: The principal, usually with teachers, makes decisions that affect the entire school.
quests.funFact: Principals often spend part of the day walking around the school to see how things are going.

quests.instruction: The principal visits your classroom during a lesson. What is the principal most likely doing?
quests.hint: Think about leading a whole school.
quests.explanation: Principals visit classrooms to see how lessons are going and to meet students.
quests.funFact: Principals often began their careers as teachers.

quests.instruction: A parent wants to talk about a serious concern after speaking to the class teacher. Who might they meet next?
quests.hint: This is the next person in charge.
quests.explanation: If a problem can't be solved at the classroom level, parents often talk with the principal.
quests.funFact: In some schools, a vice-principal or head teacher shares this role.

quests.instruction: A parent phones to say you'll be late tomorrow. Who receives the message?
quests.hint: The school's front desk handles calls.
quests.explanation: Office staff answer calls, record messages, and make sure teachers get them.
quests.funFact: School offices also handle records, forms, and visitor sign-in.

quests.instruction: You must leave school early for a doctor's appointment. Where does your parent sign you out?
quests.hint: Schools keep a record of who leaves and when.
quests.explanation: Signing out at the office lets the school know you are safely with your family.
quests.funFact: Schools keep a signing-out record so they always know who is in the building.

quests.instruction: You are joining the school next week. Which staff handle your records and forms?
quests.hint: Think about the people who handle paperwork.
quests.explanation: Office staff keep student records and help new families with forms.
quests.funFact: New students are often given a tour of the school on their first day.

quests.instruction: You've been feeling worried and want to talk to someone at school. Who is trained to listen?
quests.hint: Think about a person who helps with feelings.
quests.explanation: School counselors listen, help students with their feelings, and can suggest ways to cope.
quests.funFact: Talking about worries can make them feel lighter.

quests.instruction: Which is something a school counselor might help with?
quests.correctAnswer: Feeling nervous about a new class 😟
options: Feeling nervous about a new class 😟
Finding a book for a reading project 📚
Getting a bandage for a scraped knee 🩹
quests.hint: It's about feelings and support.
quests.explanation: Counselors support students with worries, friendships, and school changes.
quests.funFact: Counselors often work with students individually or in small groups.

quests.instruction: Your friend seems very sad for many days. What is a good way to help?
options: Ignore it because it isn't your problem 🙈
quests.hint: Some problems need an adult's help.
quests.explanation: If a friend seems upset for a long time, telling a trusted adult makes sure they get proper support.
quests.funFact: Many schools have a counselor's room where students can ask for help.

quests.instruction: Which job does a librarian do?
quests.correctAnswer: Looks after books and helps readers 📚
options: Prepares and serves meals for students 🍲
Looks after books and helps readers 📚
quests.hint: Think about what's in the library.
quests.explanation: A librarian cares for the library, orders new books, and helps students with research.
quests.funFact: Many librarians read children's books before suggesting them.

quests.instruction: A book is returned to the library. Who makes sure it goes back in the right place?
quests.hint: Think about who looks after the shelves.
quests.explanation: Books must go back to the right shelf so the next reader can find them.
quests.funFact: Library call numbers work like addresses for books.

quests.instruction: You loved a story and want more like it. Who could recommend something?
quests.hint: Think about who knows many books.
quests.explanation: Librarians know many stories and can suggest ones that match what you enjoy.
quests.funFact: Many libraries run reading clubs where readers swap recommendations.

quests.instruction: Your classmate says they feel dizzy and might faint. What is the best thing to do?
options: Ask them to run it off 🏃
quests.hint: An adult must know quickly.
quests.explanation: When someone feels dizzy, tell a teacher, who can get the nurse and make sure they sit down safely.
quests.funFact: Dizzy people should sit or lie down so they don't fall.

quests.instruction: You bumped your head slightly during PE. Why is it good to see the nurse?
quests.correctAnswer: The nurse can check that you're okay 🩺
options: The nurse can check that you're okay 🩺
The nurse will excuse you from PE for the term 🏃
The nurse will teach you the next lesson 📚
quests.hint: A bump on the head should be looked at.
quests.explanation: A nurse can check you and tell you whether you need more help.
quests.funFact: Even small head bumps should be reported to an adult.

quests.instruction: Which of these does a school nurse keep track of?
quests.correctAnswer: Students' health needs such as allergies 📋
options: How many library books each student borrowed 📚
Students' health needs such as allergies 📋
Which classes each student has on Monday 🗓️
quests.hint: It's about health.
quests.explanation: Nurses keep records of health needs so they can help the right way in an emergency.
quests.funFact: Knowing about allergies helps staff prevent emergencies.

quests.instruction: Someone spilled juice in the hallway and it is slippery. Who should you tell?
quests.correctAnswer: A teacher or the cleaning staff 🧹
options: Nobody; it will dry by itself ⏳
A teacher or the cleaning staff 🧹
quests.hint: The spill needs to be cleaned before someone slips.
quests.explanation: Reporting a spill lets staff clean it quickly, so no one falls.
quests.funFact: Wet floors are one of the most common causes of slips.

quests.instruction: Who makes sure the school building is kept clean and in good repair?
quests.hint: Think about fixing a broken door or window.
quests.explanation: Caretakers and maintenance staff keep buildings, equipment, and grounds safe and working.
quests.funFact: Many schools have caretakers who arrive before students do to open the building.

quests.instruction: Who checks that the people coming through the school gate are allowed in?
quests.hint: This person watches the entrance.
quests.explanation: Security staff help protect students by watching who comes in and out.
quests.funFact: Many schools have a gate guard or a front-desk system to check visitors.

quests.instruction: Who helps students cross a busy road safely near school?
quests.hint: This person stands near the road with a sign.
quests.explanation: A crossing guard stops traffic so students can cross safely.
quests.funFact: Crossing guards often wear bright clothing so drivers can see them.

quests.instruction: What does the bus driver need students to do while the bus is moving?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay seated and use a calm voice 🪑
options: Walk around and talk to friends 🚶
Stay seated and use a calm voice 🪑
quests.hint: The driver must be able to focus on the road.
quests.explanation: Staying seated and speaking calmly helps the driver focus on driving safely.
quests.funFact: On a moving bus, standing up can cause falls if the driver brakes suddenly.

quests.instruction: You are not sure which stop is yours. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask the driver before the bus moves 🙋
options: Ask the driver before the bus moves 🙋
Get off at the stop where most friends leave 🚏
Stay on until the bus is empty and ask then 🚌
quests.hint: Ask someone who knows the route.
quests.explanation: Asking at the start lets the driver or helper show you the correct stop.
quests.funFact: Knowing your stop in advance makes your trip safer and less worrying.

quests.instruction: Who teaches the rules of a game and helps a team practice?
quests.hint: This person gets teams ready.
quests.explanation: A coach teaches skills, rules, and teamwork, so the team can play well together.
quests.funFact: Good coaches often point out what players did well, not just their mistakes.

quests.instruction: The coach says to warm up before the game. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: It gets your muscles ready and safe 🏃
options: It tells the other team that you are ready to play 📣
It makes sure the game lasts the full time ⏱️
It gets your muscles ready and safe 🏃
quests.hint: Think about stretching and slow running.
quests.explanation: A warm-up gets your muscles ready, so you can play safely.
quests.funFact: Warm-ups usually include light jogging and gentle stretches.

quests.instruction: Who makes sure a match is played by the rules?
quests.hint: This person watches the match and makes calls.
quests.explanation: Referees and umpires help games stay fair by enforcing the rules.
quests.funFact: Referees use signals and whistles so players know what happened.

quests.instruction: You want to learn how to play the recorder. Which teacher will teach you?
quests.hint: Think about the instrument.
quests.explanation: Music teachers teach rhythm, singing, and instruments.
quests.funFact: The recorder is one of the first instruments many students learn.

quests.instruction: Who can show you how to mix colors and use brushes?
quests.hint: Think about painting.
quests.explanation: Art teachers show you techniques and help you try new ideas.
quests.funFact: The color orange was named after the fruit.

quests.instruction: Who guides a class when they plant seeds to see how they grow?
quests.hint: It's an experiment about living things.
quests.explanation: Science teachers help students ask questions, observe, and learn from experiments.
quests.funFact: In an experiment, you change only one thing at a time to keep the test fair.
